taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Bori-police-station, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 150 | 1.23 | 1.23
2 | 97.1 | 6.21 | 7.44
3 | 284 | 37.5 | 45
4 | 700 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Bori-police-station, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report — Bori-Police-Station, Bori Metropolis**

The interpreted VES model at this station comprises four layers. The resistivity sequence from surface downward is 150 Ω·m (0–1.23 m), 97.1 Ω·m (1.23–7.44 m), 284 Ω·m (7.44–45 m), and 700 Ω·m (below 45 m, unbounded). This gives a resistivity pattern of decrease-then-increase-then-increase with depth.

Applying standard curve-type notation: layers 1-2-3 (150 > 97.1 < 284) yield an **H** segment, and layers 2-3-4 (97.1 < 284 < 700) yield an **A** segment, giving a combined curve type of **HA**. This matches the classification recorded on file for this station, confirming the interpreted geoelectric sequence is consistent with a resistive basement underlying a low-resistivity layer sandwiched between two higher-resistivity units — typical of a weathered/fractured zone overlying competent bedrock.

No discrepancy was found between the computed curve type and the filed classification. The model appears internally consistent and suitable for drilling guidance.

{"curve_type_stated": "HA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
